title: Perimeter, shared edges and boundary effects
transcript: Perimeter is the total length of the boundary. When two pieces share an edge, that edge no longer lies on the outside. A cut can create a new boundary. Follow the edge of any hole if the question says to include it.

In AMC practice, a stepped outline or connected unit squares can hide which edges should be counted. Mark shared edges. A Rossmoyne style question may make several cuts. Compute how each cut changes the boundary length.
A rectangle is twelve metres wide and nine metres tall. What is its perimeter? Trace around the outside to see how many of each side length there are.
There are two sides of length twelve and two of length nine. Add all four. The perimeter is forty-two metres. Length uses metres, even though the shape also has an area.
Draw six unit squares in a horizontal row. Add two more unit squares stacked directly above its leftmost square. What is the perimeter of this shape? Count the contacts between pairs of squares.

Taken separately, the eight squares contribute four edge units each. There are seven shared edges. Each is counted twice in the separate square totals, once by each square touching it. The exposed boundary length is eighteen units. Check by walking around the outside of the L shape.

A square board has eight rows and eight columns of unit squares. Cut out an interior rectangle with side lengths four and one. Then remove one square at an outer corner far from the hole. Find the total boundary length, including the edge of the hole.

The original outer boundary is thirty-two. Removing one corner loses two outer edges of length one but exposes two equal inner edges. The hole adds its full perimeter, twice four plus twice one. Every side of the hole meets the remaining board. Add that to thirty-two. The new total boundary length is forty-two units.

A boundary is an edge with a filled cell on one side and an unfilled part on the other. This includes the through-hole boundary. The outer walk and the inner walk are disjoint. Adding their lengths keeps every requested edge once.

A shared edge disappears from the exterior twice when you start by adding all individual perimeters. Cutting around a hole creates a boundary inside the shape. Include it if the problem asks for the total boundary.

Mark shared and exposed edges with different colours. The units for perimeter are units of length. For a change of shape, list which old edges disappear and which new ones appear before re-counting everything.
